deep.reconstruction:
Context: Riemann, 'Gleichgewicht der Electricität auf Cylindern mit kreisförmigem Querschnitt und parallelen Axen'. This is Weber's fair copy, Werke XXV. The previous page reduced the Dirichlet problem on a plane domain S, bounded by n curves, to a conformal map. One takes a function ζ(z) that is real on every boundary curve and has one simple pole on each. It maps S onto an n-sheeted surface T over the upper half ζ-plane.

This page:
(1) Problem restated on T. Find a function u = Re(f), with f single-valued on T (branched with T), harmonic inside T, taking prescribed values on the n boundary lines of T. These boundary lines are the copies of the real axis in the n sheets.

(2) Green's function. Take ϖ = h + i g, analytic on T, with a logarithmic singularity at an interior point ε. Its imaginary part g is continuous on T except at ε and vanishes on ∂T. So g = log|ζ − ε| + regular, i.e. g is the Dirichlet Green's function, negative inside. Green's theorem (Grundlagen Art. 10) then gives
  u(ε) = −(1/2π) ∮_{∂T} u ∂g/∂p ds,
where p is the inward normal. This is the Poisson/Green representation formula.

(3) Construction of g by doubling (Schottky double). Reflect T across the real axis: over the lower half-plane add the mirror image of each sheet. The result is a closed n-sheeted surface over the whole ζ-sphere.
- Image reading: it has 4n−4 simple branch points. These are the 2n−2 interior branch points of T and their mirror images. The Euler-characteristic count χ(S) = 2 − n = n·1 − b gives b = 2n − 2 for T.
- Riemann–Hurwitz, p = w/2 − n + 1 with w = 4n − 4, gives genus p = n − 1 (Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen, Art. 7 and 12, pp. 106, 112).
- ϖ is then a normal Abelian integral of the third kind on this surface. It has logarithmic singularities at ε and at the conjugate (mirror) point ε', with opposite coefficients, so g ~ log|ζ − ε| − log|ζ − ε'|.
- All its periods are real, so g = Im ϖ is single-valued. By the reflection symmetry, g vanishes on the real axis.
- The 2p real conditions (real periods) fix the p complex coefficients of the added first-kind integrals. So ϖ is determined up to an additive constant.
- The Dirichlet problem is therefore solved once ζ(z) is known.

(4) Specialisation. Let ∂S consist of n circles. Either all circles lie outside one another (S unbounded), or one circle encloses the others (S bounded). The two cases are exchanged by inversion (reciprocal radii).

(5) Continuation (begun here, finished on the next page). Once ζ(z) is known in S, it is continued across each boundary circle. One assigns to the inverse point z* of z with respect to that circle the conjugate value of ζ(z). Iterating gives the Schottky-type reflection-group extension.
errors: No mathematical error on the page as read from the image. The count '2n−2' in the machine transcription is a misreading; the image shows '4n−4', which is correct.

Correspondingly, the previous page's 'n−2 Verzweigungspunkte' for T is presumably also a misreading of '2n−2'. With n−2 the doubled surface would not have genus n−1. Check: for n = 2 (annulus), T is 2-sheeted with 2 branch points.
Implicit, not stated: Riemann's normalisation that g ~ +log|ζ−ε| (negative inside) and that p denotes the inward normal. This makes the minus sign in u_ε = −(1/2π)∫u ∂g/∂p ds correct.

results.what: Green's-function (Poisson) representation of the solution of the Dirichlet problem on the branched surface T
results.modern_name: Green's representation formula / harmonic measure via Dirichlet Green's function
results.usually_credited_to: Green (1828); Riemann's Grundlagen (1851) for Riemann surfaces

results.what: Doubling an n-connected bordered surface by reflection to get a closed surface of genus n−1; Green's function as imaginary part of a third-kind integral with poles at ε and its mirror point ε', normalised to real periods
results.modern_name: Schottky double; Green's function from normalised Abelian integral of the third kind

results.what: Reduction of the circular multiply connected domain problem by inversion, and continuation of ζ by repeated reflection in the boundary circles
results.modern_name: Schottky group / reflection principle for circular domains

deep.surprise_reason: This page is Weber's redaction published as item XXV in Riemann's Gesammelte Werke (1876). Its content (Schottky double of genus n−1, Green's function via a real-normalised third-kind integral, circle-domain reflections) is known and credited to Riemann as a precursor of Schottky.

checkable.asserts: For T = upper half-plane (n=1), the formula u_ε = −(1/2π)∫u ∂g/∂p ds with inward normal reproduces the Poisson kernel; expression simplifies to 0.
Riemann's genus formula p = w/2 − n + 1 with w = 4n−4 branch points on the n-sheeted doubled surface gives p = n−1 (result 0).

checkable.asserts: Euler characteristic count shows T has b = 2n−2 interior simple branch points (not n−2).
The doubled Green's function log|ζ−ε|−log|ζ−ε'| is harmonic away from ε, ε' (result 0).
